title: A Dream: Bardo Void, Detachment, and MallWorld
content: A few weeks ago I had probably my most potent Mallworld dream I've ever had: I had a daughter in the dream, I don't have one in real life, but she was like really important to me, really intelligent, and all of these evil entities in the mall were after her. So it's this big epic struggle to keep her safe. And just as one of the most dangerous and brutal and undefeatable entities breaks through the door where we are, all of a sudden all the lights went out and all the sound went out. And as I adjusted or tried to adjust my eyes, I realized that it wasn't just the lights that had gone out, the whole scene went dark. There was nobody there, no daughter, no monsters, nothing. And I went out into the hallway, sort of the second floor hallway of the mall, and I sat in the dark and it was so quiet and so still, and it was just this total surrender where I actually was at peace. Like the drama was done, the oh-so-important daughter was gone, like she had never really existed in the first place. And the darkness... as much as I tried to adjust my eyes to see something, it would double down, insisting on its own totality. It was showing me that the whole game was an illusion. It was asking me if I could be peaceful in the on-off of it all, the on-off switch of reality itself. Real until it isn't. I've had a few NDEs (to put it mildly) and am building a framework of reality based on my experience (close to Buddhism and Gnosticism but not entirely) and this dream for me speak so much to the projection-of-mind nature of reality as I know it and a the Buddhists speak about it. In the Bardo of the afterlife we are challenged to recognize the drama as our own creation and detach from it. I believe that this is what this dream was testing me for and I suspect all of our Mallworld dreams have something to do with mastery over this liminal afterlife state.
